findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in the reports bucket (including the seeded vendor roster) are not guaranteed to be encrypted with a managed KMS key.

The bucket declares no acl and no public access block or bucket policy, relying entirely on account defaults; combined with the absence of any restriction it risks unintended public or cross-account object exposure.
No logging block is configured, so read/write access to this data bucket is not recorded, hindering detection and forensic investigation of unauthorized access.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects can be silently overwritten or deleted by an attacker with write access with no recoverable prior version.
The ledger exports bucket holds financial export data but defines no server-side encryption configuration, leaving stored objects without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for this financial data bucket, so access to ledger exports leaves no audit trail.
Versioning is disabled, so ledger export objects can be overwritten or destroyed without the ability to recover previous versions.
The model artifacts bucket has versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so artifacts are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No server-side encryption is configured for the runbooks bucket, which typically contains operational procedures and potentially sensitive internal details.
No logging block is configured, so access to operational runbook content is not auditable.

The acl value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid S3 canned ACL (it appears to be a corrupted 'log-delivery-write'), so the intended access control on the audit log bucket will not be applied as expected, potentially leaving it with unintended permissions.

The audit log bucket, which receives access logs from other buckets, has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and no bucket policy enforcing TLS-only access, so audit records could be exposed or transmitted in cleartext.

The seeded vendor roster object (likely containing supplier PII/commercial data) is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument into a bucket that itself has no default encryption, so it is stored unencrypted.
